sentences.show: A stroke left the American president paralysed. And his wife decided what reached him.
It struck on this day in 1919.
Wilson had just toured the West, selling his League of Nations.
His health broke, and he came home.
Then the stroke. Left side paralysed. Right eye, half blind.
His wife Edith and his doctor hid how bad it was.
Every paper now went through her.
She chose what was important, and when he would see it.
The Secretary of State held cabinet meetings without him. Edith pushed him out.
She said she never made a single decision.
One historian says she was, essentially, the nation's chief executive.
Wilson still won the Nobel Peace Prize, for the League.
His own country never joined it.
